lead: The McCabe-Thiele method counts the theoretical stages of a binary column on a y-x diagram, as a staircase between the equilibrium curve and two straight operating lines; a feed line fixes where the two sections meet. It assumes constant molar overflow, which keeps the lines straight, and it is the quick tray count engineers make before a rigorous simulation.
prereq: You need VLE and relative volatility, flash balances and simple distillation balances.

sections.h3: Rectifying line, stripping line and q-line

blocks.text: In the rectifying section above the feed, liquid L flows down and vapour V rises. The reflux ratio is R = L/D, where D is the distillate molar flow. Constant molar overflow keeps L and V constant in this section. A balance around the top gives the rectifying operating line.

blocks.where: y is vapour mole fraction of the more volatile component; x is liquid mole fraction; R = L/D is the reflux ratio; x<sub>D</sub> is distillate mole fraction. The line passes through (x<sub>D</sub>, x<sub>D</sub>).

blocks.text: Below the feed, the stripping section has its own operating line. It passes through (x<sub>B</sub>, x<sub>B</sub>), where x<sub>B</sub> is the bottoms mole fraction, and through the point where the rectifying line meets the feed line. A balance around the bottom gives it.

blocks.where: L′ and V′ are stripping-section liquid and vapour molar flows; B is bottoms molar flow; x<sub>B</sub> is bottoms mole fraction.

blocks.text: q measures the thermal state of the feed. It is the heat needed to turn 1 mol of feed into saturated vapour, divided by the molar latent heat. For a feed between its bubble point and its dew point, q also equals the moles of liquid formed per mole of feed. The feed line, or q-line, is:

blocks.where: x<sub>F</sub> is feed mole fraction; q is the feed thermal state defined above; the slope of the line is q/(q−1). The q-line passes through (x<sub>F</sub>, x<sub>F</sub>).

items: q = 1: saturated liquid, vertical line x = x<sub>F</sub>.
q = 0: saturated vapour, horizontal line y = x<sub>F</sub>.
0 < q < 1: two-phase feed, line slopes down from (x<sub>F</sub>, x<sub>F</sub>).
q > 1: subcooled liquid, slope q/(q−1) is positive and greater than 1.
q < 0: superheated vapour, slope q/(q−1) is positive and less than 1.

blocks.text: The q-line is not an operating line. It only locates the intersection P of the two operating lines.

sections.h3: Staircase between equilibrium and operating lines

blocks.text: Use a y-x diagram. The equilibrium curve for constant relative volatility α is:

blocks.where: y* is vapour mole fraction in equilibrium with liquid x; α is relative volatility; x is liquid mole fraction. Solved for x, this gives x* = y / [α − (α−1)y], the liquid in equilibrium with a vapour of composition y.

blocks.text: Draw the diagonal y = x. Mark x<sub>D</sub>, x<sub>F</sub> and x<sub>B</sub> on it. Draw the rectifying line from (x<sub>D</sub>, x<sub>D</sub>) to the q-line. Draw the q-line through (x<sub>F</sub>, x<sub>F</sub>) with slope q/(q−1); for a saturated liquid feed this is the vertical line x = x<sub>F</sub>. Its intersection with the rectifying line is P. Draw the stripping line from (x<sub>B</sub>, x<sub>B</sub>) through P.

items: Move horizontally left to the equilibrium curve. This gives x*, the liquid mole fraction in equilibrium with the vapour of composition y at that height.

Move vertically down to the operating line in use. Keep the rectifying line while x is above x<sub>P</sub>, the x-coordinate of P. When a horizontal step takes x below x<sub>P</sub>, switch to the stripping line. Only for a saturated liquid feed (q = 1) does x<sub>P</sub> equal x<sub>F</sub>.
Repeat horizontal to equilibrium, vertical to operating line.
Stop when x ≤ x<sub>B</sub>. Each horizontal step to the equilibrium curve is one equilibrium contact; the vertical move only sets up the next step, and the final step may be horizontal alone.

blocks.text: The final step that crosses xB is the partial reboiler, which is itself an equilibrium stage; do not add it again. Real trays outnumber the theoretical stages because tray efficiency is below one (see tray efficiency).

sections.h3: Why the lines are straight; use and limits

blocks.text: Constant molar overflow assumes equal molar latent heats, negligible heat of mixing, and negligible sensible heat. One mole of vapour condensing then supplies one mole of liquid vaporising. L and V stay constant in each section, so the operating lines are straight.

The method gives the theoretical stage count at a chosen R. A lower R moves the operating lines closer to the equilibrium curve, so more stages are needed. At minimum reflux the steps never reach xB (see reflux ratio). If CMO fails, use the enthalpy method (see Ponchon-Savarit).
The construction is used for binary columns, for checking rigorous simulation results, and for seeing how feed condition shifts the operating lines.

figure.caption: The worked example stepped off by computer from the same equations: α = 2.5, x<sub>D</sub> = 0.95, x<sub>B</sub> = 0.05, saturated-liquid feed at x<sub>F</sub> = 0.40 and R = 2. The operating lines meet on the vertical q-line; stage 7 straddles it and is the feed stage, and stage 13 (the reboiler) passes x<sub>B</sub>.

spec.aria: y against x diagram with the equilibrium curve for alpha 2.5, the diagonal, the rectifying and stripping operating lines meeting on a vertical q-line at x 0.40, and a staircase of 13 steps from x 0.95 down past 0.05, with steps 1, 4, 7, 10 and 13 numbered.

examples.question: A binary distillation column separates a mixture with constant relative volatility α = 2.5. Feed is saturated liquid with x<sub>F</sub> = 0.40, distillate x<sub>D</sub> = 0.95 and bottoms x<sub>B</sub> = 0.05 (all mole fractions of the more volatile component). Reflux ratio R = 2.0. (a) Write the rectifying operating line. (b) Find the feed intersection. (c) Write the stripping operating line. (d) Estimate the theoretical stages including the reboiler.
steps: Rectifying slope: R/(R+1) = 2/(2+1) = 0.6667. Intercept: x<sub>D</sub>/(R+1) = 0.95/3 = 0.3167. Rectifying line: y = 0.6667x + 0.3167.

Saturated liquid feed means q = 1, so the q-line is vertical at x<sub>F</sub> = 0.40. At this x the rectifying line gives y<sub>F</sub> = 0.6667(0.40) + 0.3167 = 0.5833. Feed point P = (0.40, 0.5833).
Equilibrium vapour at x<sub>F</sub> is y<sub>F</sub>* = 2.5(0.40)/[1 + 1.5(0.40)] = 1.00/1.60 = 0.6250. P lies below the equilibrium curve, as it must.

Step from (0.95, 0.95). First horizontal: y = 0.95 gives x* = 0.95/[2.5 − 1.5(0.95)] = 0.8837. First vertical to the rectifying line: y = 0.6667(0.8837) + 0.3167 = 0.9058. The table continues the staircase.
Stage 7 is the first whose liquid (x = 0.3693) falls below x<sub>F</sub> = 0.40, so it straddles the q-line: it is the optimum feed stage, and from there on the vertical moves use the stripping line.

Stage 13 gives x = 0.0322 < x<sub>B</sub> = 0.05, so the staircase ends there. Stage 13 is the partial reboiler; the column holds 12 ideal trays. The last step is about half used ((0.0675 − 0.05)/(0.0675 − 0.0322) = 0.50), so the exact count is about 12.5.
examples.answer: Rectifying line y = 0.6667x + 0.3167; stripping line y = 1.5238x − 0.0262; 13 theoretical stages including the reboiler (12 ideal trays), feed on stage 7 from the top.
examples.check:
alpha = 2.5
xF = 0.40
xD = 0.95
xB = 0.05
R = 2.0
rect_slope = R / (R + 1)
rect_int = xD / (R + 1)
y_feed = rect_slope * xF + rect_int
yF_eq = alpha * xF / (1 + (alpha - 1) * xF)
strip_slope = (y_feed - xB) / (xF - xB)
strip_int = xB - strip_slope * xB
def eq_x(y):
    return y / (alpha - (alpha - 1) * y)
x = xD
y = xD
stages = 0
while x > xB + 1e-12:
    x_eq = eq_x(y)
    if x_eq >= xF:
        y_op = rect_slope * x_eq + rect_int
    else:
        y_op = strip_slope * x_eq + strip_int
    stages += 1
    x = x_eq
    y = y_op
    if stages > 100:
        break
print(round(rect_slope, 4))
print(round(rect_int, 4))
print(round(y_feed, 4))
print(round(yF_eq, 4))
print(round(strip_slope, 4))
print(round(strip_int, 4))
print(stages)

traps: Stepping horizontally to the operating line instead of the equilibrium curve. The horizontal move gives the equilibrium liquid x* at the current vapour y; the vertical move gives the next operating-line y.
Counting the partial reboiler twice, or not counting it at all. The last step that crosses x<sub>B</sub> includes one equilibrium stage for the reboiler.
Treating the q-line as an operating line. It only locates the feed intersection P; the operating lines are the rectifying and stripping lines.

Switching operating lines at x<sub>F</sub> when the feed is not saturated liquid. Switch where the step passes x<sub>P</sub>, the x of the operating-line intersection; x<sub>P</sub> = x<sub>F</sub> only when q = 1.

quiz.q: In the McCabe-Thiele method, what does q represent?
quiz.a: q is the heat needed to turn 1 mol of feed into saturated vapour divided by the molar latent heat. For a feed between bubble point and dew point it also equals the moles of liquid formed per mole of feed.

quiz.q: Why is the q-line drawn through the point (x<sub>F</sub>, x<sub>F</sub>)?
quiz.a: Every q-line is the feed-stage balance written for the passing streams. When x = x<sub>F</sub> the balance is met only by y = x<sub>F</sub>, so every q-line, whatever the feed condition, passes through (x<sub>F</sub>, x<sub>F</sub>).

quiz.q: For x<sub>D</sub> = 0.95 and R = 2.0, write the rectifying operating line.
A staircase crosses x<sub>B</sub> after 13 horizontal steps. A student says the column has 13 theoretical stages without the reboiler. Correct the statement.
quiz.a: The 13 steps already include the last equilibrium contact at the bottom, which is the partial reboiler. The column has about 13 theoretical stages including the reboiler, not 14.

quiz.q: State the constant molar overflow assumptions.
quiz.a: Equal molar latent heats, negligible heat of mixing and negligible sensible heat; L and V are constant in each section.

quiz.q: What is the q-line for a saturated vapour feed with x<sub>F</sub> = 0.40?
quiz.a: q = 0, so the q-line is horizontal at y = x<sub>F</sub> = 0.40.

quiz.q: Why do the rectifying and stripping operating lines intersect on the q-line?
quiz.a: The feed is added at the feed stage. A balance around that stage must satisfy both section balances at the same feed composition and feed condition, so the two operating lines meet on the q-line.

quiz.q: In the worked example, which stage receives the feed, and how do you know from the staircase?
quiz.a: Stage 7. Stage 6 leaves liquid x = 0.4162, still above x<sub>F</sub> = 0.40; stage 7 leaves x = 0.3693, below it, so stage 7 straddles the q-line. Switching lines there gives the fewest stages.

beyond: Not for the exam. Simulators solve rigorous stage models, but McCabe-Thiele stays the fast check for binary columns; a spreadsheet can automate the staircase. Search "McCabe-Thiele spreadsheet" and "constant molar overflow".
